_about: Triggering cases. See README.md in this folder. `skill` is the description under test; `expected` is the skill that should be picked first (null: none of this repo's skills). Only `train` cases may be read while editing a description.

split.method: random, stratified: one of every three cases per (skill, should_trigger) held out
split.added: 2026-11-20: 36 cases for six development skills whose descriptions changed (agent-brief, architect-deep-dive, devils-advocate, tyr-verdict, refactor-review, nexus), split the same way with seed 20261120; no earlier case moved; 2026-11-21: 30 cases for the five database skills that had none (dbquery, dbpropose, dbbuild, dbdiagram, dbarchitect), split the same way with seed 20261121; no earlier case moved

cases.prompt: The CSV export on the invoices page puts the tax column in the wrong place since yesterday's deploy. Everything else works, but finance needs it right before they close the month tomorrow. Can you get a fix out today?

Customers with an apostrophe in their surname get a 500 when they save their profile. Site is otherwise fine. Support has had about a dozen complaints this morning, so I want this patched and shipped this afternoon.
Prod bug, not an emergency but annoying: the password-reset email links to the staging domain. Find it, fix it properly and get it released before end of day.
Checkout has been returning 502s for the last twenty minutes and the error rate is still climbing. We're losing orders. Help me get this under control.
The nightly billing job double-charged a few hundred customers last night and it will run again in three hours. What do we do?
There's a typo in the footer, it says 'Copyrigth'. Fix it whenever, it can go out with the next regular release.
I just got paged. The API is timing out for everyone in the EU region and the status page is lighting up. Where do we start?
Someone noticed that the admin audit-log endpoint has been answering without authentication since the last release. It is live right now. Need to deal with this immediately.

We shipped a quick patch for the rounding bug on Monday, but the monthly revenue report is still off by thousands and now the ledger table has rows that don't balance. This looks bigger than we thought.
The date picker on the booking form shows Sunday as the first day of the week for Spanish users. It is live and a client complained. Nothing is broken otherwise. Can we patch it today?

Last Thursday's outage is fully resolved and the fix has been in for days. I need the written account of what happened between the 12th and the 14th for the client, from the commits and the Slack export in docs/incident/.
What's the difference between an SLO and an SLA? Two or three sentences is enough.
Here's the schema dump of the ERP database we inherited (schema.sql). Before we decide anything, tell me how good or bad it is and where the risks are.
Can you go through db/structure.sql and grade the data model? I want strengths, weaknesses and a number I can compare against after we clean it up.
We're about to take over maintenance of a client's Postgres database. I've put the DDL in client-ddl/. Give me an honest assessment of its quality, I'm not asking you to change anything.
We're starting a clinic appointment system: patients, practitioners, rooms, bookings, cancellations. What tables do we need? Give me the schema for Postgres.
This report query takes 40 seconds. I've pasted the EXPLAIN ANALYZE output into plan.txt. Why is it slow and what should I change?

The assessment of the orders database is done and so is the target model with its diagrams. Now I need the plan to get from one to the other that the client can sign off on: what we change, in what order, how each step is rolled back.
Model this domain for me: a library with members, copies of books, loans, reservations and fines. I want proper keys and constraints, running on SQL Server.
The review of our inventory schema came back with a pile of normalization problems (report in audit/report.md). Redo the schema so those go away.
Is this table design in third normal form? orders(order_id, customer_id, customer_email, product_id, product_name, qty, unit_price). If it isn't, show me what it should look like.
Take a look at legacy.sql and tell me how much trouble this database is in. I only want the evaluation and a score for now.
Product search is getting slow on Postgres. Should we add Elasticsearch next to it, or just put Redis in front? Which one ends up owning the product data?
The database proposal was accepted on Friday (proposal/proposal.md). Write the SQL scripts that create it.
Can you look over the changes on feature/rate-limiter before I merge it into main? Tell me whether it's safe to merge.
Marta opened a pull request for the new refund flow, it's the top commit range on origin/refunds. Go through it properly and write the comments I should leave on it.
I addressed the comments from the last round on the payments branch. Check the new commits and tell me if anything is still wrong.
My branch is done. Write the pull request description for it and tell me if I should break it into smaller PRs before I ask anyone to look at it.
Ignore the production code on this branch. I only care about the tests that came with it: would they actually fail if the behaviour broke?
Explain what `git rebase --onto` does, with a small example.
I've finished the work on feature/audit-export. Get it into shape so a colleague can go through it: clean up the commits and write up what it does and how to verify it.
This branch ended up at about 1,200 changed lines with a refactor mixed into the feature. How should I cut it up before I open it for the team?

Dani asked me to look at their pull request on origin/notifications, but I can't tell what it's supposed to do. Before I spend an hour on it: is it in a state where it can be looked at at all, or should I send it back?
Go through the diff between main and feature/cache-layer and find the bugs. File and line, how bad each one is, and whether you'd merge it.
PR 212 was merged yesterday after a long discussion. Write up what was decided in that discussion and what happened to each comment, so we can find it later.
We just tagged v2.4.0. Write the changelog entry our customers will read.
Log a bug for the login timeout problem we just found: sessions expire after 5 minutes instead of 30. Put it in the current sprint.
I spent three hours today on the SSO migration task. Record that against it and move it to In Review.
Here are the six problems QA found this afternoon (qa-notes.md). Get each of them into the tracker, and don't duplicate ones that are already there.
Our board has about 140 open items and nobody knows what to pick up next. Go through it and tell me what state it's in and what order things should go in.
We have one giant epic called 'Customer portal'. Help me cut it into pieces we can deliver and demo one at a time, with a first release that works end to end.
What's the difference between a story and a task in Scrum? Short answer please.
Planning is on Thursday. Go through the next batch of work in the tracker and get it ready: anything too big gets cut down and everything needs criteria we can check.
Everything on the board has been 'in progress' for weeks and nothing gets finished. Look at the board and tell me why work is stuck.
We're starting the supplier onboarding initiative from scratch. Lay out the whole user journey and tell me what goes into the first release and what waits.
Close the item about the broken PDF export, it shipped this morning. Link the commit that fixed it.
Raise a task for upgrading the Node version on the build agents and assign it to me.
List what shipped in this release in language a customer would understand, for the 'what's new' panel in the app.
The design for the refund-window feature is settled and recorded under .workflow/designs/. Write the build plan from it so we can start building test-first.
We've agreed how rate limiting should work: per API key, a 429 with Retry-After, limits in config. Now write the brief: ordered acceptance criteria, where to test, what's out of scope.

I need a spec for this feature before anyone codes it. It's CSV import for contacts, and the decisions are all made: sync under 5,000 rows, duplicates matched on email, a per-account limit. Turn them into something a developer can build against, criterion by criterion.
We want to add CSV import for contacts but nothing is decided yet: sync or async, what to do with duplicates, what the limits are. Work the design with me before we plan anything.
The build plan in .workflow/brief.md is approved. Turn its acceptance criteria into failing end-to-end tests before we write any code.
Write up a Jira story for the CSV import feature, with acceptance criteria, and put it in the next sprint.
Design this with me: we need multi-currency support in invoicing. I don't want code yet, I want the decisions made properly.
Before we build the notification service I want an architecture review. What are the trade-offs between a queue and a cron poller, and where should the boundaries go?
We're about to add tenant-level feature flags. Work the design: take me through the open questions a few at a time, with the options and what each costs to reverse.
The design for tenant-level feature flags is done and recorded in the repo. Write the build plan from it, with the criteria in the order we should build them.
Model this domain for me: clinics, practitioners, appointments and invoices. What tables do we need, with keys and constraints?
In a couple of paragraphs, what's the difference between hexagonal architecture and clean architecture?
I just finished the cutoff feature and the tests are green. Tear this apart before I ship it: assume it's wrong and show me where.
Red-team this change. What did we miss? I want every edge we didn't handle, with evidence for each.
The suite passes on what we just built, but I don't trust it. Are the tests lying? Try to falsify them.
Review this PR for bugs: Dani's branch origin/export-filters against main. File and line for each, and whether you'd merge it.
The teardown left six findings in the ledger. Go through them, decide which are real, and tell me go or no-go.
Red-team the design for our new login flow before we build it: who would attack it, how, and what should we require of it?
The teardown is done and its findings are in .workflow/ledger.md. Adjudicate the findings: which are real, which are noise, and what do we have to fix.
Is this ready to merge? The adversarial pass raised eight issues on the cutoff change. Weigh each one against its evidence and give me a go/no-go.
Triage the teardown from this morning. Cut the false claims and turn the confirmed defects into fix slices we can build test-first.
The feature is built and cleaned up. Now assume all of it is wrong and hunt for defects. I want the harshest pass you can do before anyone makes the final call.
Is Marta's pull request ready to merge? Go through the diff on origin/refunds and give me your recommendation.
Is my branch ready for someone to look at? Check the description and tell me whether I should split it first.
The TDD cycle is done and everything is green. Check what I just built for code smells and clean it up before we move on.
Refactor before merge: look at the diff on this branch for duplication and long methods, and apply the behaviour-preserving fixes with the tests run between each one.
Clean up after TDD. The new rules module works but it's ugly. Structure only, don't change what it does.
Review this PR for bugs: origin/cache-layer against main. I want correctness problems with file and line, not style.
Which parts of this codebase are the worst to work in? Find the hotspots: the files that change often and are complex.
Rename the variable `tmp2` to `pending_orders` in billing/export.py.
Increment 3 splits into four PRs. Coordinate the sessions: brief each one, keep track of where they are, and bring me their questions in one batch.
I've got five slices to build and I want to run these in parallel, one session per pull request. You orchestrate the sub-sessions and don't write the code yourself.
Be the harness for this migration: several sessions will each build a PR through the full pipeline, you judge them on what they recorded, and nothing merges without my go.
Build the cutoff feature from the brief, test-first, one slice at a time.
We have 30 open items for the billing rewrite. Split the next release into thin stories and tell me what order to pull them in.
Run the test suite and the linter at the same time and tell me which one fails.

Our order history page got slow after the last release. pg_stat_statements output and EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) for the top statements are in perf/. Which statements cost the most and what should we change?
The dashboard view fires about 300 SQL queries per page load; the ORM's query log is in logs/sql.log. Review the SQL it's generating and tell me what's wrong.
The DBA wants to add four indexes (perf/proposed-indexes.sql). Using last month's Query Store export in qs/, tell me which ones actually help the workload and which only slow down the inserts.
Here's the full DDL of our warehouse database (ddl/warehouse.sql). Grade the schema itself, keys, normalization and constraints. We don't have any query logs.
We need tables for a ride-sharing app: drivers, riders, vehicles, trips and ratings. Design the schema for MySQL with proper keys and constraints.
What's the difference between a LEFT JOIN and an INNER JOIN? A short example is enough.

We have the audit report (audit/report.md), the target design (design/) and both diagrams. Write up the recommendation for the steering committee: which changes, in what order, what each one risks, and what we still have to decide.
Turn these findings and the new data model into a migration plan the client can approve before anyone writes DDL. Every step needs a rollback and a way to check it worked.

Our legacy billing database has orphaned rows and no foreign keys, and the redesign is finished. What should we actually do, and in what order, without breaking the nightly jobs? I need a document for sign-off, not SQL.
The migration plan was approved yesterday (proposal/proposal.md). Generate the .sql files for PostgreSQL 16.
Before we plan anything I need to know how healthy the schema in legacy/schema.sql is. Score it and list its weaknesses.
Draw the ER model and the relational model for the design in design/model.md as draw.io files.
Proposal accepted (proposal/proposal.md, with the design in design/). Generate the DDL scripts for SQL Server 2022 in the order they have to run.
The client signed off on the new schema. Write the CREATE TABLE, constraint and index scripts for SQLite, with a few negative tests that prove the constraints reject bad rows.
Everything's approved. Turn the accepted plan into ordered .sql files for Postgres that we can review and apply ourselves. Don't run them.
The audit and the target model are done. Before any SQL gets written I need the plan the client signs: the decisions, their order, and a rollback for each step.
Nothing is designed yet, there are only the requirements in docs/requirements.md for a school enrolment system. What should the tables be?
An UPDATE in our nightly batch locks the table for ten minutes. The plan and the slow log are in batch/. Why does it happen, and how should we rewrite it?
Draw the entity-relationship diagram for design/model.md in Barker notation, plus a relational diagram with every table, key and foreign key, as editable draw.io files.
Our old ER diagram uses Chen notation (described in docs/er.md). Redraw it in Oracle CASE*METHOD notation.
Make me a schema diagram from schema.sql that I can edit in diagrams.net, with the tables, columns, primary keys and foreign keys.
Here are the requirements for a veterinary clinic (docs/requirements.md). Work out the entities, keys and normal forms, and give me the DDL.
Draw our office network as a draw.io diagram: two VLANs, the firewall, and the site-to-site VPN to AWS.
Look at the DDL in db/schema.sql and tell me whether the relationships are modelled correctly. Grade it and don't change anything.

We're splitting the monolith. Orders live in Postgres, the team wants MongoDB for the catalogue and Kafka between services. Which store should own each piece of data, and how do the others stay in sync?
Our request handlers write to Postgres and then to Redis and Elasticsearch, and the three keep disagreeing. What should the data architecture be?
Analytics dashboards are hammering the primary database. Should we add a read replica, a warehouse or something else, and how stale can each report afford to be?
We've settled on Postgres as the only store. Now design the tables for subscriptions, invoices and payments with proper keys.
One endpoint is slow, and its EXPLAIN output shows a sequential scan over 20 M rows. What index or rewrite fixes it?
Give me a compose file that runs our API with Postgres and Redis locally, with health checks so the API waits for both.
